refine.variant: SHAP/LIME terms AND stability phrases AND perturbation terms AND tabular terms (V1)
refine.decision: Too narrow: the perturbation concept removed most benchmark papers.

refine.variant: SHAP/LIME terms AND single-word stability terms AND perturbation terms AND tabular terms (V2)
refine.decision: Single words such as stable/robust add noise; recall still low.

refine.variant: SHAP/LIME terms AND single-word stability terms AND tabular terms, no perturbation concept (V5)
refine.decision: Too broad to screen: stability words often describe model performance, not explanations.

refine.variant: Stability words in title AND (SHAP/LIME terms AND tabular terms) in title/abstract (V6)
refine.decision: Better recall (the only variant that found Hwang et al. 2025) but still broad; the free OpenAlex API budget then ran out, so OpenAlex was used for piloting only.

refine.variant: SHAP/LIME terms + 19 stability phrases + perturbation terms + tabular terms (T2)
refine.decision: Dropped the perturbation concept: it lost benchmark papers.

refine.variant: SHAP/LIME terms + 19 stability phrases + tabular terms (T1)
refine.decision: Adopted. The phrase-level stability concept was then used in every database.
ScienceDirect matched quoted phrases loosely; switched to braces for exact phrases and split into SD1-SD3 because of the 8-connector limit.
Prefix matching added noise (e.g., "shap" matched "shape"); switched to exact words with $.
